HistoricalSummary: St. Andrew's opened the recovered portion of the 2003 golf archive with a 165-191 win over Patrick Henry Academy at Penny Branch Golf Club in Estill, S.C. Davy Clay led the Saints with a 36, followed by Josh Smith at 38, Andrew Chapman at 43, and Lyle McKenzie at 48.
On Mar. 12 at Wilmington Island Golf Club, Thomas Heyward defeated St. Andrew's 165-184. Davy Clay shot 42, Josh Smith 43, Travis McGinley 48, and Chris Brinker 51 for St. Andrew's.

The March 26 Savannah Morning News reported a three-team match at Indigo Run Golf Club: Hilton Head Prep 165, Hilton Head Christian 168, and St. Andrew's 181. Davy Clay shot 39 and Josh Smith 41 for the Saints.

At Santee National Golf Club on Apr. 1, St. Andrew's shot 171 in a SCISA region tournament round behind Holly Hill Academy's 158 and Beaufort Academy's 162. Clay led the Saints with a 37, while Chris Brinker and Travis McGinley shot 44 and Smith shot 46.

At the SCISA State Golf Championship on Fripp Island, St. Andrew's finished sixth in the 12-team field with a two-day score of 722. Josh Smith shot 85-83-168, Davy Clay 94-76-170, Travis McGinley 93-98-191, and Chris Brinker 95-100-195. The final Savannah Morning News 9-hole averages listed Clay at 38.5 over four matches and Smith at 42.0 over four matches.

StatusNote: The Spring 2004 archive includes recovered match reports from March and April, with team results and available St. Andrew's individual scores from 10 matches and tournament events.
HighlightNotes: Davy Clay tied for fifth individually at the SCISA Class AA State Tournament after shooting 90-70-160.
HistoricalSummary: St. Andrew's finished third at the SCISA Region 2-AA Final on Apr. 22, 2004 at Santee National Golf Club, shooting 325 behind Holly Hill's 307 and Beaufort Academy's 315.
Davy Clay led St. Andrew's with a 78, followed by Josh Smith at 80, Drew Aimone at 82, and Steve Carbone at 85. Samantha Long also shot an 86.

Clay and Smith made the All-region team. Beaufort Academy's Mark Anderson was the medalist with a 66, and the report noted that the first round of the state tournament would be played Apr. 26-27 at Fripp Island.

At the SCISA Class AA State Tournament at Ocean Point Golf Club on Fripp Island, St. Andrew's finished fourth in the 12-team field with a two-round 352-328-680. Davy Clay tied for fifth individually at 90-70-160, while Drew Aimone shot 80-83-163, Samantha Long shot 89-91-180, Steve Carbone shot 93-89-182, and Josh Smith shot 99-86-185.

HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2005 golf archive now includes recovered match reports beginning with a Mar. 29 multi-team match at Belfair Country Club, where St. Andrew's shot 173 behind Hilton Head Prep's 147 and tied Beaufort Academy. Drew Aimone led St. Andrew's with a 39, followed by Thomas Withers at 41, Samantha Long at 46, and Ashley Long at 47.
On Mar. 30, St. Andrew's defeated Patrick Henry Academy 173-185 at Wilmington Island Golf Club. Samantha Long shot 41, Drew Aimone 42, Kevin Crouch 44, and Ashley Long 46.

At Eagles Point Golf Club on Apr. 5, St. Andrew's shot 160 in a five-team match won by Hilton Head Prep. Samantha Long led St. Andrew's with a 34, while Drew Aimone shot 41, Ashley Long 42, and Thomas Withers 43.

At Crescent Pointe Golf Club on Apr. 12, St. Andrew's shot 163, one stroke behind Hilton Head Christian and 13 behind Hilton Head Prep. Drew Aimone and Thomas Withers each shot 39, Ashley Long 42, and Samantha Long 43.

At the Apr. 21 SCISA 2-AA championship at Colleton River Club, the first nine holes counted as a makeup region round. Drew Aimone shared medalist honors with Hilton Head Christian's Matt Raehn at 36, and St. Andrew's shot 162 to qualify for the AA state tournament along with Beaufort Academy.

In the 18-hole SCISA 2-AA championship, St. Andrew's finished third at 323 behind Hilton Head Prep and Beaufort Academy. Thomas Withers earned medalist honors with a 75, and Withers, Aimone, and Samantha Long were named all-tournament.

St. Andrew's stood second after the first round of the SCISA AA state tournament at Ocean Creek Golf Course, shooting 334 behind Beaufort Academy's 329. The Saints finished fourth with a two-day total of 679.
